purpose: R1.13.1 — the ONE bounded finding from Posidon's independent review of R1.13: findStoryCandidatesByFingerprints carried LIMIT 9 with NO ORDER BY, so the PRE-LIMIT page selection was not deterministic — with 12 owners of one digest, a changed scan direction could return a DIFFERENT set of 9 owners for the SAME stored data (and zero writes), changing the final 8 candidates. Posidon demonstrated the violation on real local workerd D1 (counterexample: 1 failed, exit 1; a temporary ORDER BY value ASC made it pass; their experimental change was fully reverted — no fixed code was ever committed by Posidon). THE FIX (the only production change this round): the lookup statement now carries `ORDER BY value ASC` BEFORE LIMIT — for a fixed kind and digest the value is `sc1:<digest>:<storyId>`, so this order IS the (kind,value) primary-key order of the probed range: SQLite satisfies it directly from the same range index scan (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN verified: SEARCH on the PK index, no full scan, no temporary b-tree sort), and the probe page becomes the SAME first-9 rows regardless of scan direction or physical insertion order. UNCHANGED BY CONTRACT: the number of lookups (at most 3, one per present signal), the probe 9 / cap 8 limits, fencing, the sc1 namespace, no merge, and the whole candidate-discovery honesty boundary; entity aliases, semantic matching, the reader contract, the provider policy, and the schema (still 3, ZERO new DDL) do not change. TESTS (red→green recorded on the real path): (1) the main counterexample on real workerd D1 — 12 owners of ONE digest, the final candidate set must be IDENTICAL between a normal lookup and a lookup under PRAGMA reverse_unordered_selects with permuted (descending) seed insertion order; RED on the base (2 failed | 12 passed in the suite: the reversed scan selected 03..10 while the normal scan selected 00..07 — a different 8 with identical data), GREEN after the fix (14/14); (2) EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN of the REAL shipped statement captured on the real pipeline path with REAL binds — range SEARCH on the PK index, no SCAN, no TEMP B-TREE, and the ORDER BY precedes LIMIT in the shipped SQL; RED on the base, GREEN after; (3) the concurrency window PROMISED in R1.13, now covered — two stories sharing ONE fingerprint, both lookups run BEFORE either commit (the second story's whole real path runs inside the first story's provider-call window), then both commits: both stories/drafts/fingerprint owner rows survive, NO overwrite and NO unique failure, and both reports claim ONLY their lookup moment (no_candidates_observed + the lookup_moment_visibility limitation), never completeness. HONEST LIMITATION RECORDED: PRAGMA reverse_unordered_selects is a LOCAL workerd D1 capability used as an honesty probe for unordered SELECTs; no Cloudflare-production PRAGMA behavior is claimed or required. VERSION SYNC 1.8.0 -> 1.8.1 across ALL active references (package.json; package-lock.json ROOT metadata ONLY — dependencies untouched; wrangler.jsonc APP_VERSION root+preview; phase0 DEFAULT_APP_VERSION; .env.example; .dev.vars.example; tests/helpers/test-env.ts; the active test assertions). The test:db subset now ALSO runs tests/integration/story-candidates.test.ts and tests/integration/story-candidates-demo.test.ts (they were already part of the full suite; their absence from the SUBSET was never a testing gap — the fresh subset count is deliberately NOT folded into prior product totals).
